The new `make` skill is committed (`08af2e3d0`): it replaces `naming` and `new-page`, so one skill now covers creating any file, folder, page, class or name.

### 🧱 make `.claude/skills/make/SKILL.md`
Four questions in order, then the page steps:
- **Name it:** what was `naming`, shortened. Brainstorm with cheap agents, pick the clearest name, plural folders only for collections.
- **Place it:** your new rule. A file about a module lives in that module's folder, and a strictly AI class lives under `framework/ai`. It also says where task records and scratch go, and that every new file must be linked.
- **Class it:** one class per file, architecture written first; the detail stays in the `code` skill.
- **Show it:** every class gets a live view of its own state, shown beside the rendered page.

I applied it directly: the decisions are the same, plus your one new rule, and you had asked twice. Nothing was deleted. The old `new-page` text sits word for word in `make/page.md`, and both old skills are in `.claude/skills-archive/` with a line saying why. The other choice was keeping three skills and only adding the placement rule. The `minion`, `code`, `page` and `skill-improvement` skills now point to `make`.
